questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Malawi?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Malawi on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: It has borders with the countries of Tanzania, Zambia, and Mozambique.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Malawi on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Malawi on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Malawi?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: The capital of Malawi is Lilongwe and the spoken languages are English and Chichewa.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Lilongwe?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Malawi is Lilongwe.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Lesotho about 30,355 square kilometres; Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres; Rwanda about 26,338 square kilometres.
